title: The European Aftermarket in 2035: The Winners Are Being Determined Now
gist: BCG projects the European automotive aftermarket to grow at just 1.7% CAGR to EUR 116 billion by 2035 (versus 4.7% in 2021-2025), as an aging, slower-growing car parc, falling mileage and a rise in BEVs to 26% of the parc strip out routine maintenance volume. Value per repair visit, not vehicle throughput, becomes the growth engine, while fleets (20% of the parc by 2035), insurers (70% of collision work) and online platforms take control of demand, and AI capability separates winners from a structurally disadvantaged rest.

insights.claim: The European automotive aftermarket is forecast to grow at a 1.7% CAGR through 2035, less than half the 4.7% CAGR recorded from 2021 to 2025.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Reset top-line growth assumptions for listed European parts distributors and suppliers: the sector's recent growth rate is not the run rate.
insights.locator: As a result of these factors, we expect

insights.claim: European aftermarket revenue is projected to reach EUR 116 billion by 2035 from EUR 99 billion in 2025, measured at wholesale level excluding labor and including both the independent aftermarket and original equipment suppliers.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: A EUR 17 billion increment over ten years is the entire addressable growth pool - share shift, not market growth, is where returns come from.
insights.locator: Volume Is No Longer the Main Growth Engine

insights.claim: The historic aftermarket business model in which more cars mechanically meant more repair work is described as obsolete, with value per repair shop visit replacing vehicle volume as the growth engine.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Screen aftermarket operators on revenue per workshop visit and attach rate, not on vehicles serviced or outlet count.
insights.quote: Volume is giving way to value and integrated ecosystems are replacing one-to-one transactional relationships.
insights.locator: The Time to Act Is Now

insights.claim: By 2035 the European aftermarket is expected to be both more digitally dependent and more concentrated than today, with customer access channeled through digital platforms and AI-enabled interfaces.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Structural consolidation implies a multi-year M&A pipeline and margin expansion for scaled, digitally integrated players; sub-scale independents are the supply.
insights.locator: By 2035, the aftermarket will be more dependent

themes.theme: Car Parc Math and Electrification Drag

insights.claim: The European car parc is projected to reach 343 million units by 2035, but growing at only a 0.4% CAGR versus 1% from 2021 to 2026.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Unit growth contributes almost nothing to aftermarket demand this decade; the bull case must rest on price and content per car.
insights.locator: Aging Car Parc. High new-vehicle prices

insights.claim: By 2035 more than one-third of vehicles on European roads are projected to be older than 16 years, up from 23% in 2021, as high new-vehicle prices push consumers toward used ICE cars and longer holding periods.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: An older parc favors independent repair chains and value/private-label parts over OEM-tied service networks - a positive offset to EV-driven volume loss.
insights.locator: Aging Car Parc. High new-vehicle prices

insights.claim: Total kilometers driven across European vehicles remains below the 2019 level because of weaker passenger vehicle usage, even though light commercial van mileage has risen above 2019, and kilometers per vehicle are projected to shrink 0.6% per year through 2035.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Wear-and-tear parts demand is in structural per-vehicle decline; van and commercial fleet exposure is the mileage growth pocket.
insights.locator: Structural Decline in Vehicle Usage

insights.claim: Pure battery electric vehicles are projected to reach 26% of the European car parc by 2035, up from 4% in 2025, and the EV shift alone is expected to subtract roughly 0.7 percentage points from annual aftermarket growth through 2035.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: That -0.7pp is the single quantified drag on the sector; it converts EV adoption forecasts directly into aftermarket revenue estimates.
insights.locator: Electrification. This is one of the biggest forces

insights.claim: EVs cut routine maintenance demand because they have fewer moving parts, but make individual repairs more expensive because their components are more technologically complex - shifting aftermarket economics from frequency to ticket size.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Winners will be shops with high-voltage systems and thermal management capability; volume-based independents lose twice as visits fall and complexity rises.
insights.locator: Electrification. This is one of the biggest forces

insights.claim: Advanced Driver Assistance Systems will reach roughly one-third of the European car parc by 2030 and reduce collisions, cutting crash repair demand while raising per-visit value for shops equipped to do calibration once parts standardize.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Collision repair volume is a shrinking pool; calibration capability and standardized ADAS parts are where the margin migrates.
insights.locator: ADAS. The introduction of Advanced Driver Assistance Systems

themes.theme: Pricing Power and the Inflation Split

insights.claim: Annual price increases for OEM components are running more than 2.5 percentage points above general inflation in some countries, driven partly by the added complexity of electronic sensors and onboard computers in modern vehicles.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Component price inflation well above CPI is the core pricing-power argument for parts makers - and a wedge that pushes consumers toward independents and private label.
insights.locator: Vehicle Architecture. Both EVs and modern ICE vehicles

insights.claim: The average cost of a repair in Germany rose 4% between 2024 and 2025, with inflation in labor and materials cited as the main driver of aftermarket revenue growth through 2035.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Reported aftermarket revenue growth is largely a price effect; real volume trends are weaker than headline sales suggest.
insights.locator: Macroeconomic Conditions. Inflation

insights.claim: Rising repair and maintenance costs are expected to make many consumers defer repair shop visits, particularly for nonessential work, partially offsetting the revenue benefit of price inflation.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Watch deferral of discretionary maintenance as a leading indicator of aftermarket volume misses in weak consumer environments.
insights.locator: Macroeconomic Conditions. Inflation

insights.claim: Inflation is bifurcating the aftermarket because stronger players can pass rising costs to consumers while weaker ones must absorb them, so the sector's aggregate markup rises far less than input inflation.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Do not model sector-wide margin expansion from inflation; pass-through ability is the differentiator between winners and casualties.
insights.quote: As a result, the overall rise in players’ markup is far lower than inflationary effects.
insights.locator: Macroeconomic Conditions. Inflation

insights.claim: The new Euro 7 component standard, taking effect later in 2026 with tougher specification, durability, and environmental monitoring requirements, is expected to work in the aftermarket's favor by raising the quality bar and reinforcing demand for compliant high-spec replacement parts.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: A regulatory quality floor is a share-shift catalyst toward compliant premium suppliers and against the cheapest imported parts.
insights.locator: A Changing Regulatory Landscape Offers New Opportunities

insights.claim: Updated EU regulations on end-of-life vehicles and batteries raise the compliance burden for parts suppliers and repair shops, making position within emerging circularity value chains a strategic decision rather than a compliance chore.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Compliance cost is a fixed-cost barrier that accelerates consolidation and rewards players who monetize remanufacturing and recycling.
insights.locator: A Changing Regulatory Landscape Offers New Opportunities

insights.claim: The Motor Vehicle Block Exemption Regulation and emerging data access rules continue to protect the independent aftermarket's access to vehicle data, repair information, and spare parts markets.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: The independent channel's survival is a regulatory construct; any weakening of MVBER or data access rules is an existential risk worth monitoring.
insights.locator: A Changing Regulatory Landscape Offers New Opportunities

insights.claim: Fleet-owned vehicles are forecast to reach 20% of the European car parc by 2035, up from 8% in 2021, concentrating repair purchasing decisions in professionalized, cost-conscious buyers.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: A 2.5x rise in fleet share means B2B procurement pressure on workshop pricing; independents without fleet contracts lose access to the fastest-growing demand pool.
insights.locator: Fleets and Insurers Are Becoming More Powerful

insights.claim: Insurance companies handle around 70% of collision-related repairs and allocate that work through claims management platforms and preferred networks, giving them decisive control over which repairers get the job.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Insurer network inclusion is effectively a licence to operate in collision repair; exclusion from claims platforms is a demand cliff.
insights.locator: Fleets and Insurers Are Becoming More Powerful

insights.claim: Winning fleet and insurer business requires repair shops to integrate their systems into the fleets' and insurers' own IT systems and digital ecosystems, a bar that smaller aftermarket players will struggle to clear and that risks excluding them from a growing segment.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: IT integration capability, not workshop quality, becomes the gating factor for demand access - a hidden capex line for small operators and a consolidation driver.
insights.locator: Both fleet operators and insurers impose new requirements

insights.claim: Fleet and insurer work is stable and high-volume but comes with standardization demands, little operational flexibility, and tight margins for the repairer.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Revenue quality matters: workshop chains skewing to fleet/insurer channels should be underwritten on lower structural margins than independent retail work.
insights.locator: Both fleet operators and insurers impose new requirements

insights.claim: Private-label components, typically manufactured outside Europe, have grown to roughly 20% market share across EMEA over the past five years, driven by the purchasing power of emerging buyer groups.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: A one-fifth private-label share is a direct margin and volume threat to established tier 1 branded parts makers - track brand mix disclosure closely.
insights.locator: Private Labels Are Gaining Relevance

insights.claim: Online platforms are disintermediating wholesalers by building direct supplier and repair shop relationships and letting shops source cheaper third-party parts worldwide using databases of exact technical specifications, wiring diagrams, and benchmark diagnostic approaches.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Traditional parts distribution faces an Amazon-style intermediation risk; wholesaler multiples should embed platform share loss over the next decade.
insights.locator: New Digital Entrants as a Market Trend

insights.claim: Compliance costs, margin pressure, and the capital needed for EV and digital capability investment are making the rationale for M&A across the aftermarket value chain more urgent.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Expect an accelerating deal pipeline across European distribution and workshop chains; sub-scale assets become sellers, not compounders.
insights.locator: Market Consolidation Is Continuing

insights.claim: Most European aftermarket players today have little understanding of AI or treat it merely as an efficiency tool, even though AI is becoming the sector's core technology - a gap framed as the decisive competitive variable.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: The stated adoption gap means AI capability is currently underpriced as a differentiator among aftermarket incumbents; look for the few players actually redesigning operations.
insights.quote: AI is rapidly becoming a core technology for the whole sector, but most players today still have little understanding of AI or treat it as an efficiency tool.
insights.locator: To stay competitive in this challenging environment

insights.claim: By 2035 the aftermarket winners will be those that use data and AI to strengthen the customer relationship rather than those that simply repair the most vehicles.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: The competitive KPI shifts from throughput to customer lifetime value; assess management on data assets and retention, not bay utilization.
insights.quote: We believe that by 2035, the winners will be those that use data and AI to strengthen the customer relationship rather than simply repairing the most vehicles.
insights.locator: To stay competitive in this challenging environment

insights.claim: An AI-first operating model means redesigning work around human-AI collaboration in which agents handle execution and humans provide oversight and judgment, making the shift an organizational challenge as much as a technological one.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Organizational redesign, not model access, is the bottleneck - a filter for separating credible AI narratives from press-release AI in industrials.
insights.locator: An AI-First Operating Model

insights.claim: The recommended entry point for AI adoption is to identify the single biggest operational constraint - demand forecast accuracy, technician scheduling, or customer communications - and apply AI to that bottleneck first.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: A concrete diligence question for management teams: which constraint did you point AI at, and what moved?
insights.locator: An AI-First Operating Model

insights.claim: Wholesalers are deploying AI beyond dynamic components pricing to automate warranty claims analysis and identify weak parts and shoddy installation work, while tier 1 suppliers use AI-enabled tools to identify parts accurately and cut incorrect returns.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Warranty cost and returns rates are measurable near-term AI payoffs - concrete P&L lines to check for evidence of real deployment.
insights.locator: Automating Activities Across the Value Chain

insights.claim: Leading automotive OEMs are betting that AI-driven convenience will retain customers longer and raise customer lifetime value before owners defect to cheaper independent repair shops.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: OEM service retention is the battleground; every extra year of retention is revenue taken directly from the independent channel.
insights.quote: Leading OEMs are betting on the convenience AI provides to retain customers longer, increasing overall customer lifetime value.
insights.locator: Rewriting the Rules of Customer Engagement

insights.claim: Organizations that lack AI capabilities will be at a structural disadvantage, and companies must change their operating models to capture the technology's positive compounding effects.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Treat absent AI capability as a permanent handicap in this sector, not a lag that can be closed by buying software later.
insights.quote: Organizations that lack AI capabilities will be at a structural disadvantage.
insights.locator: What Winning Looks Like

insights.claim: Vehicle connectivity will disproportionately benefit automotive OEMs and their authorized repairer networks because of their structural access to vehicle data for remote diagnostics, preventive maintenance, and over-the-air software updates.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Data access asymmetry is the durable moat in the aftermarket; independents' counter is regulated data access and third-party diagnostics.
insights.locator: Changing How Repair Shops Carry Out Maintenance

insights.claim: Aftermarket wholesalers risk being cut out of the value chain by e-commerce price pressure and by OEMs building their own service ecosystems, and must respond by becoming ecosystem orchestrators with their own digital platforms plus EV and electronic component ranges.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Wholesale distribution is the most structurally threatened link; platform buildout and EV parts mix are the metrics that separate survivors.
insights.locator: What Winning Looks Like

insights.claim: Tier 1 suppliers should expand downstream into connected diagnostics using sensors to remotely assess vehicle health, gaining diversified revenue, field performance insight into their own parts, and a stronger negotiating position against OEMs.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Downstream moves by tier 1s are both a growth story and a bargaining-power story versus OEM customers - watch for aftermarket/services segment disclosure.
insights.locator: Tier 1 suppliers should expand downstream

insights.claim: OEMs and authorized repairers hold three advantages that are hard to replicate - customer relationships formed at point of sale, access to full vehicle service history, and connectivity through their digital products.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Use this triad to judge whether an independent aftermarket player has any credible answer to OEM encroachment on service revenue.
insights.locator: Automotive OEMs and authorized repairers must capitalize

insights.claim: New OEMs, particularly from China, are entering European markets with limited aftersales infrastructure, creating partnership openings for established authorized repair networks with strong capabilities and brands.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: A concrete, near-term revenue option: European service networks can monetize Chinese OEM entry rather than only losing share to it.
insights.locator: New OEMs, particularly from China

insights.claim: Three core strengths will separate winning repair shops from the rest: technical depth for higher-value electrification-driven repairs, access to reliable sources of demand, and integration into the digital ecosystems through which demand flows.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: A three-part scorecard for underwriting any workshop chain; missing any one leg implies structural share loss regardless of scale.
insights.locator: What Winning Looks Like

insights.claim: Scale alone will no longer determine success in the European aftermarket, and must be combined with AI capability, customer relationships, and ecosystem partnerships.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Challenges the standard consolidation thesis: buying volume without digital integration does not create a winner.
insights.quote: While still important, scale alone will no longer determine success.
insights.locator: In this environment, the basis of competition will evolve

insights.claim: Northern and western European markets with high EV penetration will feel repair and maintenance volume pressure earliest and most acutely, with meaningful declines likely after 2030, while southern and eastern Europe follow the same direction more slowly.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Geographic mix is a timing arbitrage: southern and eastern European aftermarket exposure buys several years before the EV volume hit lands.
insights.locator: Market dynamics will vary by geography

insights.claim: The European aftermarket is characterized as being in a state of transition rather than decline, despite slowing volumes and electrification pressure.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Argues against a pure secular-short framing of European aftermarket names; the trade is dispersion between adapters and laggards.
insights.quote: The European aftermarket is in a state of transition, not decline.
insights.locator: The Time to Act Is Now
